claims.text: The Australian marketing industry's self-regulatory body, AANA, established an AI in Marketing Council in May 2025 and released industry guidelines on the ethical and responsible use of AI in marketing for public consultation.

sources.title: Industry Guidelines on the Ethical AI use in Marketing released for public consultation
sources.whatItMeasured: AANA announcement of the AI in Marketing Council (formed May 2025) and public-consultation release of ethical-AI-use guidelines for marketing.
sources.quote: The Council, created in May 2025, was formed to guide the marketing and advertising industry in the ethical and responsible use of artificial intelligence.

claims.scope: Australian marketing and advertising industry self-regulation. Applies to marketing practitioners including Marketing Managers; not a statutory instrument.
claims.refuteNotes: 3 of 3 skeptics failed to overturn: the AANA page is the industry body's own published announcement (HTTP 200), the population is Australian marketing practitioners and the date is 2025.

claims.text: PwC's AI Jobs Barometer finds AI is reshaping entry-level roles and creating a two-track labour market in which AI-exposed occupations grow faster and demand more advanced skills.

sources.title: AI Jobs Barometer
sources.whatItMeasured: PwC recurring analysis of labour-market and job-posting data on AI exposure and skill demand.
sources.quote: AI is reshaping entry-level jobs and creating a two-track labour market as AI-powered roles grow faster and demand advanced skills.
sources.verification: HTTP 301 redirect to a localised URL; content reachable (not 404).

claims.scope: Global PwC analysis; not Australia-specific and not limited to Marketing Managers. Indicates directional labour-market pressure on cognitively-exposed roles.
claims.refuteNotes: 3 of 3 skeptics failed to overturn: the PwC Barometer is a published recurring analysis (301 redirect, content reachable), the global population is preserved and the 2025 edition is inside the window.

claims.text: The Australian Parliamentary Library's 2025 research on AI's potential impact on the Australian labour market identifies marketing and sales among the occupations with high exposure to automation and generative-AI displacement.

sources.title: Potential impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on the Australian labour market
sources.whatItMeasured: APH Parliamentary Library Issues and Insights 2025 overview of AI's expected impact on the Australian labour market and occupations.
sources.verification: Parliamentary Library blocks scripted requests (HTTP 403, not 404); official published research product.

claims.scope: Australian national-labour-market analysis; identifies exposure at occupation-group level, not measured employment effects for Marketing Managers specifically.
claims.refuteNotes: 3 of 3 skeptics failed to overturn: the APH Parliamentary Library publication is an official research product (403 scripted block, not 404), the population is the Australian labour market at occupation-group level and the 2025 edition is inside the window.
